$comment: CLI simulator missions. setup: az commands run first (silently). checks: JMESPath queries over the simulated cloud (resourceGroups, vnets, nsgs, vms, storageAccounts, locks, history = successful commands, attempts = every command tried) that must be true.

missions.title: Your first resource group
missions.goal: Create a resource group called `rg-learn` in UK South, then list your resource groups as a table.
steps: Resource groups are the container every Azure resource lives in. Create one with `az group create`.
List them with `az group list`, and add `-o table` for a readable view.

checks.description: You listed the groups as a table

missions.title: Network foundation
missions.goal: Build the network for a web app: resource group `rg-web` in UK South, VNet `vnet-web` (10.0.0.0/16) with subnets `snet-web` (10.0.1.0/24) and `snet-app` (10.0.2.0/24), and an NSG `nsg-web` that allows inbound HTTPS (TCP 443), associated with `snet-web`.
steps: Create the resource group.
Create the VNet with its first subnet in one command: `--address-prefixes` plus `--subnet-name` and `--subnet-prefixes`.
Add the second subnet with `az network vnet subnet create`.
Create the NSG, then a rule with `az network nsg rule create` (priority, protocol Tcp, destination port 443).
Associate it: `az network vnet subnet update ... --network-security-group nsg-web`.
hints: `az network vnet create -g rg-web -n vnet-web --address-prefixes 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name snet-web --subnet-prefixes 10.0.1.0/24`
`az network nsg rule create -g rg-web --nsg-name nsg-web -n allow-https --priority 100 --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 443`

missions.title: Fix an insecure storage account
missions.goal: A legacy account `stlegacyexports` in `rg-data` allows public blob access and TLS 1.0. Lock it down: no public blob access and a minimum of TLS 1.2. Then create a new account `stsecure` + any 4 digits (for example `stsecure1234`) in the same group: zone-redundant (Standard_ZRS) StorageV2.
steps: See what is wrong first: `az storage account show -n stlegacyexports -g rg-data --query "{tls: minimumTlsVersion, public: allowBlobPublicAccess}"`.
Fix it with `az storage account update`.
Create the new account with `--sku Standard_ZRS --kind StorageV2`.
hints: `az storage account update -n stlegacyexports -g rg-data --allow-blob-public-access false --min-tls-version TLS1_2`
Storage account names are 3-24 lower-case letters and numbers, and must be unique.
setup: az storage account create -n stlegacyexports -g rg-data --sku Standard_LRS --allow-blob-public-access true --min-tls-version TLS1_0

checks.description: stlegacyexports no longer allows public blob access
A new zone-redundant StorageV2 account exists in rg-data

missions.title: A VM, start to stop
missions.goal: Create a Linux VM `vm-api-01` (Ubuntu2204, size Standard_B2s) in a new group `rg-compute` in West Europe. Look at what else `az vm create` made for you. Then stop it in the way that stops the compute bill.
steps: `az vm create` needs a name, a group and an image. For Linux, `--generate-ssh-keys`.
`az resource list -g rg-compute -o table` shows the VNet, NSG and public IP it created.
There are two ways to stop a VM. Only one releases the compute (and the charge).
hints: `az vm create -g rg-compute -n vm-api-01 --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s --generate-ssh-keys`
`az vm stop` powers off but you still pay for the compute; `az vm deallocate` releases it.

checks.description: You listed what az vm create made

missions.title: Tag for cost reporting
missions.goal: Cost reports group spending by tag. Tag the existing groups `rg-shop` and `rg-batch` with `env=prod` and `costCentre=CC-1042`, then use `az group list` with the `--tag` filter to show only groups tagged `costCentre=CC-1042`.
steps: `az group update -n <group> --tags env=prod costCentre=CC-1042` sets both tags at once (it replaces any existing tags).
`az group list --tag costCentre=CC-1042 -o table`
hints: --tags takes several key=value pairs separated by spaces.
`--set tags.env=prod` adds one tag without removing others.
setup: az group create -n rg-shop -l uksouth --tags owner=web

checks.description: rg-shop is tagged env=prod and costCentre=CC-1042
rg-batch is tagged env=prod and costCentre=CC-1042
You filtered the list by tag

missions.title: Protect production from deletion
missions.goal: Put a `CanNotDelete` lock named `do-not-delete` on `rg-prod`. Then prove it works: try to delete `rg-prod` and watch it fail. (Leave the lock in place.)
steps: `az lock create --name do-not-delete --lock-type CanNotDelete --resource-group rg-prod`
`az group delete -n rg-prod --yes` should now fail with ScopeLocked.
hints: A CanNotDelete lock still lets people change resources; ReadOnly blocks changes too.
Locks are inherited by everything in the resource group.
setup: az storage account create -n stprodorders -g rg-prod

checks.description: rg-prod has a CanNotDelete lock called do-not-delete
You tried to delete it after locking it

missions.title: Answer questions with --query
missions.goal: Three VMs already exist. Use `--query` (JMESPath) to answer: which VMs are deallocated? Print just their names, as tsv. Then print a table with only the name and size of every VM.
steps: `az vm list -d` includes `powerState`.
Filter with `--query "[?powerState=='VM deallocated'].name" -o tsv`.
Pick fields with a multiselect hash: `--query "[].{Name: name, Size: hardwareProfile.vmSize}" -o table`.
hints: Inside a double-quoted --query, use single quotes for strings.
setup: az vm create -g rg-fleet -n vm-web-01 --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s --generate-ssh-keys
az vm create -g rg-fleet -n vm-batch-01 --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_D4s_v5 --generate-ssh-keys
az vm create -g rg-fleet -n vm-jump-01 --image Win2022Datacenter --size Standard_B1ms --admin-password Simulated123!

checks.description: You filtered the VMs by power state with --query

checks.query: length(history[?contains(@, 'vm list') && contains(@, '.name') && (contains(@, '-o tsv') || contains(@, '--output tsv'))]) > `0`

checks.description: You built a name and size table
checks.query: length(history[?contains(@, 'vm list') && contains(@, 'vmSize') && (contains(@, '-o table') || contains(@, '--output table'))]) > `0`

missions.title: The same, in PowerShell
missions.goal: Switch the terminal to PowerShell. With Az cmdlets, create a resource group `rg-pwsh` in North Europe and a Standard_LRS storage account in it whose name starts with `stpwsh`.
steps: Use the PowerShell button above the terminal.
`New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-pwsh -Location northeurope`
`New-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-pwsh -Name stpwsh1234 -Location northeurope -SkuName Standard_LRS`
hints: `Get-Command` lists the cmdlets the simulator knows; `Get-Help New-AzStorageAccount` shows the syntax.

checks.description: A Standard_LRS account starting stpwsh exists in rg-pwsh
You used PowerShell to do it
